standard.title: Importance of environments to people and animals
standard.description: the importance of environments, including natural vegetation and water sources, to people and animals in Australia and on another continent
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3K05): Students compared Australia with a neighbouring country in terms of natural, managed and constructed features. From Y3 (AC9HS3K04): Students explored First Nations Australian connections to Country/Place.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the importance of natural environments, including vegetation and water, to people and animals in Australia and on another continent.

nodes.label: Types and roles of vegetation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the main vegetation types (forest, savannah, grassland, woodland, desert) and explain the important roles vegetation plays in sustaining environments.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three vegetation types and explain at least two roles vegetation plays in the environment.
nodes.typical_width: Identify forest, savannah, grassland, woodland and desert vegetation types in Australia and another continent; explore how vegetation produces oxygen, prevents erosion, retains rainfall, provides habitat, shelters crops, cools urban places, provides medicines and materials.
wider: Compare vegetation types in Australia with those of another continent (e.g. Africa or South America) and explain similarities and differences
Investigate how vegetation change (e.g. clearing for farming) has affected a specific environment
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding vegetation types and roles is prerequisite to explaining the importance of environments — functional role knowledge grounds the importance claim.

response_modes.reason: Students need to know what vegetation types exist and what they do before they can explain importance — build the knowledge base through maps and images before the explanatory demand.

success_criteria: Identifies at least three vegetation types
Explains at least two functional roles of vegetation in the environment

nodes.label: Importance of water
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain the importance of water to the environment and to sustaining the lives of people and animals.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain at least two ways water is important to people and animals in Australia.
nodes.typical_width: Identify the importance of water to the environment and human and animal survival; explore how people's connections to environments are aesthetic, emotional and spiritual as well as functional; investigate strategies to protect environments.
wider: Compare water availability and management in Australia with a contrasting continent (e.g. Africa) and discuss implications
Investigate First Nations Australian knowledge of water sources and management practices

response_modes.reason: Water importance varies enormously across Australian environments — comparing arid and tropical regions reveals the full range.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The aesthetic, emotional and spiritual dimensions of connections to environment (in addition to functional) enrich the concept of 'importance' beyond resource use alone.
success_criteria: Explains at least two ways water is important to people and animals
Includes at least one functional and one non-functional dimension of importance
